open_prs_before.head: claude/credit-timing-repair
open_prs_before.body:
Scoped deliverable for #19 requested in TEAM (`5feefa985206`): repair the credit-timing tool. Read-only analysis; **no learning-rule, learning-rate, reward, training-code or simulation change.** Base: `cc7dc83`.

**Files:** `gpu-pilot/src/noesis_gpu/credit_timing.py`, `gpu-pilot/tests/test_credit_timing.py`, `docs/workstreams/claude/credit-timing/` (README + result JSON).

**What changed (vs reviewed `bbbfd776`):** shared predictor basis (pooled unsupervised PCA applied unchanged to every birth) and the full 7-joint response with shared coefficients instead of a per-birth PCA (Codex's `[X,X]` vs `[X,-X]` counterexample reproduced in a test, plus rotation/flip invariance and birth-exchangeability tests); explicit coverage with a reason per neuron (`nerve`, `region`, `non_leg_nerve`, `region_no_consensus` for `.NO_CONS`, `region_ambiguous`, `no_side_or_region`), constant columns counted and excluded, `INSUFFICIENT_COVERAGE` legs skipped; permutation rank named `family_rank` with `rank_is_calibrated_p_value: false` and an interpretation string; provenance (SHA-256 of every log/observation file, neuron table, module, `plasticity.py`; parameters; numpy); per-birth consistency summary.

**Tests:** `NOESIS_SOURCE=<core 42c2076>/src python -m pytest gpu-pilot/tests/test_credit_timing.py` 16 passed (~50 s); full pilot suite 211 passed / 3 skipped; Ruff clean.

**Result on the three existing logs** (D3 `logged` seed 1000, C2 `train-1001`, `train-1002`; parent `9fd7d411`; 2,970 learning-active samples): 372/453 explored neurons mapped to a leg (323 by nerve, 49 by region; 66 non-leg nerves, 15 ambiguous region, 0 constant columns; the previous mapping dropped 236). No leg shows joint-velocity or learning-signal prediction above the permutation null (joint R² 0.014-0.044 vs null p99 0.055; learning signal R² 0.020-0.035 vs null p99 0.074); best lags are scattered across 0-500 ms and unstable across the three births.

**Limits:** three 5 s births; detection floor is about R² 5-7% (the null measured on these logs), so smaller effects are undetectable; descriptive only (no stationarity/exchangeability/calibration, no causal claim, a non-significant rank is not evidence that learning is absent); neuron-to-leg mapping is heuristic; coefficients assumed shared across births.

open_prs_before.title: Add opt-in synaptic depression and measure recovery without relaxing P8
open_prs_before.head: codex/synaptic-depression
open_prs_before.body:
Add opt-in short-term synaptic depression to the stateful LIF kernel and a controlled response battery on PR #13's fully FAFB/MANC-corrected brain. Finite presynaptic resources recover exactly between transmission events; U=0 keeps legacy dynamics unchanged. The first transmission retains the original signed strength and external drive is unaffected.

The 66-trial screen/replication preserves aggregate P1-P4/P7 at U=.1, tau=300 ms and terminates sustained reverberation in the tested trials. 14/15 stimulated replicates have no spikes in late recovery; the remaining trial's last spike is 537.5 ms after offset with no reactivation through 5 seconds. However, the unchanged full-window P8 still fails and sugar-to-PAM drops from 1.38 to .0285 Hz. This is not an accepted calibrated-brain fix: depression stays disabled by default, and uniform whole-brain application is explicitly a modelling assumption.

`docs/findings-depression.md` contains pre-run predictions, six-candidate seed-0 screen, fixed selection rule, three-seed control/replication, per-seed results and negative findings. Supporting CSV/JSON retains all measurements and the extended recovery trace. NT signs, region factors, body, response_battery predicates, and shared findings.md are unchanged. PR #12's sign correction remains separate to avoid mixing interventions.

Validation: ruff passes; pytest 47 passed (10 new depression tests). Historical U=0 spike times/indices match PR #13 exactly across three recurrent-network seeds with background input. Chunk boundaries preserve resources/delays; extended trace reproduces original recovery counts. All edits and caches are in C:/dev/noesis-codex-depression; main/Claude checkouts untouched.

open_prs_before.head: feature/m1-connectome-sim
open_prs_before.body:
## What
First working vertical slice: the FlyWire whole-CNS connectome simulated as a spiking network, validated, and coupled to a physical fly body. Nothing is learned.

- **Connectome -> sparse signed matrix** (158k neurons, 1.5M pairs; pairs <5 synapses dropped, sign from predicted neurotransmitter).
- **Event-driven LIF simulator** (numba, stateful, active-set kernel) with Shiu et al. 2024 parameters.
- **Validation:** driving sugar-taste neurons activates the proboscis motor neuron MN9 (needs ~200 Hz drive).
- **Body:** leg motor neurons -> NeuroMechFly joints via FlyWire muscle annotations; leg afferents driven by joint angle/contact.
- ADR-0001, `docs/findings.md`, CI (ruff + pytest), 11 tests.

## Honest status
The embodied fly does **not** walk: it flips onto its back after the brain "wakes". Some motor neurons lock at hundreds of Hz (the simple LIF model has no adaptation). See `docs/findings.md`. Single runs, no statistics yet.

## Assumptions (all configurable)
ACh excitatory; GABA/Glu/histamine inhibitory; monoamines/unknown excitatory. Muscle->joint signs and sensory transfer functions are modelling choices, not data.
